investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pods remained stuck for 140–145 seconds before the eval timed out and returned empty evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota on the only two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt fails immediately with Unschedulable, preventing the eval runner from reaching the agent creation, VM-readiness, or runtime steps. Because the pod never starts, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is written, and all contract assertions fail. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool in the production-api environment; no eval infrastructure or source-code defect is indicated by the available evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck 142s, latencyMs=147583 — confirms the failure is not isolated to a single probe invocation.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck 145s, latencyMs=151886 — all three checks across the feature share the same scheduler rejection.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the pod never reached a running state, so the runner could not write orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent returns.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=146881, well below the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000, confirming the eval did not time out on latency — it failed on scheduling rejection.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota exhausted on the two eligible nodes: existing remote-agent VMs or peer-pods are consuming all available slots, leaving none for new probe pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message.

Node pool under-provisioning: only two nodes in the cluster carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource label, and neither has spare capacity. A cluster scaling event, node failure, or deliberate scale-down could have reduced available slots to zero.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on four of six nodes: the pod spec requires a node label or taint that only two nodes satisfy, concentrating all scheduling pressure on those two nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall.

Leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in the runner) failed in a previous run, orphaned VMs may be occupying the resource quota.
Cluster-level resource quota or LimitRange applied to the eval namespace capping kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations below the node's physical capacity.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod creation attempt was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource are fully exhausted, and the remaining four nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner could not create a remote agent, and therefore produced zero evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run (2026-07-01T21:53–21:58Z), 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote-agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported it as fully consumed, and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is an accurate signal of this infrastructure condition; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident is present in the packet beyond the eval results themselves.

Secondary: Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes — the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 are at capacity. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or the eligible node pool has not scaled, this compounds the capacity problem.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pods remained stuck for 140–145 seconds before the eval timed out and returned empty evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota on the only two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt fails immediately with Unschedulable, preventing the eval runner from reaching the agent creation, VM-readiness, or runtime steps. Because the pod never starts, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is written, and all contract assertions fail. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool in the production-api environment; no eval infrastructure or source-code defect is indicated by the available evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck 142s, latencyMs=147583 — confirms the failure is not isolated to a single probe invocation.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck 145s, latencyMs=151886 — all three checks across the feature share the same scheduler rejection.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the pod never reached a running state, so the runner could not write orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent returns.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=146881, well below the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000, confirming the eval did not time out on latency — it failed on scheduling rejection.
source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: remote-agent-create is marked required=true and degradedAfterFailures=1, meaning a single failure triggers a degraded signal for the feature.
possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota exhausted on the two eligible nodes: existing remote-agent VMs or peer-pods are consuming all available slots, leaving none for new probe pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message.

Node pool under-provisioning: only two nodes in the cluster carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource label, and neither has spare capacity. A cluster scaling event, node failure, or deliberate scale-down could have reduced available slots to zero.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on four of six nodes: the pod spec requires a node label or taint that only two nodes satisfy, concentrating all scheduling pressure on those two nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall.

Leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in the runner) failed in a previous run, orphaned VMs may be occupying the resource quota.
Cluster-level resource quota or LimitRange applied to the eval namespace capping kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations below the node's physical capacity.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~140–145 s across all three sibling checks), preventing any agent lifecycle step from executing and leaving all required eval evidence fields empty.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning only 2 nodes are even eligible, amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall. If the selector was recently narrowed or node labels changed, capacity that previously existed may now be unreachable.

Tertiary — cluster-level resource quota or limit range on kata.peerpods.io/vm: a quota ceiling may have been reached cluster-wide, preventing any new peer-pod VMs from being allocated even if node-level capacity appears available.

Quaternary — concurrent eval or workload contention: multiple eval runs or production workloads may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, transiently exhausting capacity during the eval window. The near-identical stuck durations across all three sibling checks (140s, 142s, 145s) suggest the condition persisted across the full eval sequence rather than being a brief transient spike.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available and unused on the 2 affinity-matching nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and an alternative (e.g., admission webhook rejection, network policy, or runtime class misconfiguration) must be investigated.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after freeing no resources succeeds and the pod schedules normally, the failure was a transient capacity spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are shown to have been recently relabeled or had their affinity labels removed intentionally, the root cause shifts to a node label/affinity configuration change rather than capacity exhaustion.

If the remote-agent pod spec's node affinity selector is shown to have changed (e.g., targeting a node group that no longer exists or was renamed), the scheduling failure is a configuration drift issue rather than a capacity issue.
If local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) are also failing with the same scheduler message, the problem may be broader than the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource class alone.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity across all cluster nodes and warns when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), before pod scheduling failures occur.

Add an eval that detects and alerts on stale or leaked remote agent pods (pods in Pending or Running state beyond a maximum expected lifetime) to prevent capacity exhaustion from accumulated eval artifacts.
Consider adding a sibling check that verifies node label consistency for the remote agent affinity selector, alerting if the number of eligible nodes drops below a minimum threshold.
